note: Ratchet for scripts/check-entry-budget.mjs. entryJsGzBytes pins the current entry weight and may only go DOWN; targetGzBytes is the 350 KiB v1.0 budget from RELEASE-GATE.md. `history` is newest-first: it replaced a chain of loweredOn/previousLoweredOn/previouslyLoweredOn/priorLoweredOn keys that had run out of adjectives, and no key beyond the two numbers above is read by anything.

loweredOn.by: deferring the ⌘K palette, and moving three lazy-surface key groups out of the eagerly bundled `common` catalogue
loweredOn.measured: 294,902 bytes (288.0 KiB gz), down from 303,457 measured on the same inputs — 8,555 bytes gz out of the entry, and 62.0 KiB under the 350 KiB v1.0 target.
loweredOn.why: The gate went RED by 6,096 bytes after the 2026-09-08 commit wave (plans 34-42). The prevailing guess was @xyflow/react, the non-tree-shakeable diagram library the schema designer had just added — and attributing the entry source map, per the 2026-08-18 lesson, showed it is NOT IN THE ENTRY AT ALL: its lazy import holds, as do all five new dashboard surfaces. The guess was wrong for the sixth time in this file's history, and for the same reason every earlier one was: it reasoned from what the wave had just added instead of from the chunk.

whatItActuallyWas.1. the en-US catalogue, -5,562 KiB gz: `common` is bundled into every user's first load, and the wave grew it 1,378 -> 1,738 keys. 422 of those keys belong to surfaces that cannot render on a first paint: `common.dataio.*` (207 — import wizard, exports manager, export builder), `common.files.*` (69 — the Files library), and `common.email.*` (143), which is the starkest case of all: every one of those 143 call sites is in apps/server's email-template machinery, so a dashboard user was downloading text their browser can never render. They are the `dataio`, `files` and `email` namespaces now. Same shape as 2026-09-01's `studio` split, and the third time this exact defect has been found — a lazy surface's strings landing in the eager namespace.
whatItActuallyWas.2. the command palette, -2,993 KiB gz: AppShell mounted `CommandPaletteHost` unconditionally with `paletteOpen` initialised to false, so the entry carried the palette body, @adminium/ui's CommandPalette and the Radix Dialog family behind it purely so a modal could render nothing on every route for every user. Same argument as the 2026-08-27 first-run wizard and the 2026-08-24 scheduled-reports manager. ⌘K had to move to AppShell first: the shortcut has to work before the chunk exists, and the host held the app's only `useCommandK` call.

loweredOn.threeKeysDidNotMove: `dataio.import.title` and `dataio.exports.title` are read by `data-io/routes.tsx`, which the router imports STATICALLY and which is therefore in the entry — the Topbar problem from the studio split, verbatim. Both were byte-identical to `common:nav.imports`/`nav.exports`, so that module reads the twins and the two keys are deleted. `files.uploadsUnavailable` went the same way: its reader is the page-files TEMPLATE, which renders inside a user-built page that would never await the namespace, and the widget already falls back to a byte-identical `ui:templates.files.uploadsUnavailable`. Overrides on all three are COPIED to the surviving twin by meta migration 0029, in 0022's shape.
loweredOn.theServerHadToLearnToLoadThem: `createServerI18n` initialised with EAGER_NAMESPACES only, and no server path called `loadNamespaces`. Moving 143 keys into a deferred namespace would therefore have rendered silent English for every non-English email recipient — silent because every call site supplies a defaultValue, so there is no missing-key error to see. Fixed in `packages/i18n/src/server.ts`, at the shared factory rather than in a caller, because there are TWO wrappers and the second (`translatorForLocale`) is the built-in template SEEDER: patching only the first would have written English rows into `adminium_email_templates` for seven locales.
loweredOn.theTestThatCouldNotFail: `email-templates-routes.test.ts` computed its expected value through the same createServerI18n + renderStarter path it asserted against, so both sides would have degraded to English together and stayed green. It reads the literal from `locales/<tag>/email.json` now. A new gate, `apps/server/test/email-fallbacks.test.ts`, covers what the four dashboard *Namespace.test.ts guards structurally cannot: they all anchor on cwd=apps/dashboard, and all 143 of these call sites are in apps/server. Verified to have teeth by injecting a drift.
loweredOn.headroom: 2,000 bytes — the usual minifier-drift margin, not growth room.
loweredOn.estimateVsMeasurement: The i18n move measured 5,838 bytes in isolation and 5,562 as part of the pair. Sum-of-parts over-counts a gzipped bundle, as the 2026-09-01 icon entry recorded (estimate 2.1 KiB, measurement 1,574 B) — the analysis says which line to pull, the build says what it is worth.
loweredOn.attributedAgain: Per the 2026-09-01 corollary. On the new entry's own source map: `resources/en-us/{dataio,files,email}.js` attribute ZERO bytes, `en-us/common.js` fell 69,943 -> 54,134 raw, CommandPalette / CommandPaletteHost / the Radix Dialog family attribute zero, and `palette/recent.ts` correctly REMAINS (AppShell imports `pushRecent` directly). index.html still references one script and zero modulepreload links, so the deferred chunks are genuinely outside the gate's asset set.
loweredOn.cost: One chunk fetch the first time /imports, /exports, the export builder or /files is opened, behind the Suspense boundary each already had; and one the first time ⌘K is pressed. A non-en-US locale is ahead on every route and behind only on the surface it opens.
loweredOn.whatIsStillThere: zod is 74.2 KiB raw in the entry, reachable from the boot path through `api/pages.ts` and `api/widgetData.ts` -> @adminium/engine/config. Deferring it MEASURED 22,082 gz bytes — by far the largest remaining lever — and was deliberately not taken here: it makes `parsePageDocument` async and touches the page-document reader's never-crash rules, which is a correctness change, not a bundle change. Recorded so the next pass does not have to re-measure it.

history.by: the add-on nav rail and its route (51b/51c) — owner-ratified, after both removable parts were removed and measured
history.measured: 297,329 bytes (290.4 KiB gz) against 296,902 (289.9 KiB) on the same inputs — +0.5 KiB gz — set to 299,329 with the usual 2,000-byte margin. 59.6 KiB under the 350 KiB v1.0 target.
history.why: An add-on may now contribute a rail row and a page route, so SidebarNav gained a row list and the router two entries. Neither can be lazy-loaded: they ARE the shell, and a rail that arrives after the first paint is the regression this budget exists to prevent. Two parts of the first version's weight could be removed and were, before this raise was asked for: the host runtime used `import * as ui` on three libraries, which widened what its lazy chunk shared with the others until Rollup hoisted the page-builder into the entry (2.2 KiB gz, attributed through the source map after the first guess was wrong), and the host's own strings sat in the eager `common` namespace when only the lazy page host reads them (0.85 KiB raw, now the deferred `addOns` namespace). What is left is 1.2 KiB raw of SidebarNav and 0.4 KiB of router.tsx.

history.by: excluding the page-builder's private glyph vocabulary from gen-icon-core.mjs's best-effort `icon:` sweep
history.measured: 295,361 bytes (288.4 KiB gz), down from 296,935 measured on the same inputs — 1.5 KiB gz out of the entry, and 62.6 KiB under the 350 KiB v1.0 target.
history.why: The record directly below named this as the follow-up and this is it. `scripts/gen-icon-core.mjs` collects two ways: declared vocabularies (STRICT_SOURCES) and a best-effort sweep of every `icon:` literal under SCAN_ROOTS. The sweep's comment claimed over-collecting costs nothing because a fabricated name is dropped against lucide's catalogue — true of a WRONG name, false of a right one. A name lucide really has is emitted, and an emitted name is a static import in the ENTRY chunk whether or not anything resolves it there.
history.whatItActuallyIs: Replaying the generator's collection with a per-name origin map found EIGHTEEN of the 144 emitted names whose only origin was `packages/widgets/src/templates/page-builder/builder-config.ts` — AlarmClock, Award, BadgeCheck, Coins, Heading, History, Minus, MousePointerClick, MoveVertical, PanelBottom, PenLine, QrCode, Repeat, Sigma, SquareCheckBig, SquareDashed, Text, TicketPercent. They are unreachable from the entry by construction: `BLOCK_KIND_META`'s `.icon` is read only by `BlockIcon` in `PageBuilder.tsx`, which resolves through the LOCAL static-import map `BLOCK_ICONS` and never through `CORE_ICONS` or `lucideByName`. Its host `EmailTemplatesPage` is one of the eleven routes the 2026-08-18 record moved behind React.lazy — so a lazy surface's private vocabulary was riding in every user's cold boot. The generator's own docblock already named the page-builder as a local-map vocabulary that must not be forced onto the catalogue's spelling; the sweep just had no way to act on it. `SWEEP_IGNORE` is that way, and it skips the `icon:` sweep ONLY — a `<Icon name>` or `lucideByName()` in the same file would still be collected, because those genuinely do resolve through this set.
history.theEstimateWasHigh: The analysis that opened this priced the 18 at ~2.1 KiB gz and the measurement is 1,574 bytes. Two reasons, both worth keeping. `Minus` is imported by name in `packages/ui/src/components/checkbox/Checkbox.tsx`, so dropping it from `CORE_ICONS` removed an object-literal key and no module at all; and gzip shares a dictionary across lucide's very similar path data, so eighteen removals do not cost eighteen icons' worth. Sum-of-parts over-counts a bundle every time — the estimate said which line to pull, the build said what it was worth.
history.headroom: 2,000 bytes — the usual minifier-drift margin, restored. The record below had it down to 1,556 by the end of the same day.
history.cost: Nothing at runtime. All eighteen still RESOLVE: `icon-resolver.ts` loads the full catalogue on demand for a name outside the core set, which is the designed fallback for an icon an admin hand-picks by searching. None of the eighteen is in either IconPicker's curated grid, in the engine's SHAPE_ICONS, or in any archetype nav, so no first paint reaches for one — verified with the same origin map.
history.theOtherHalf: The over-collection hid a second defect and fixing one without the other would have let the generator re-collect it. `BLOCK_ICONS` had 22 keys against `BLOCK_KIND_META`'s 28: the six `email.*` slugs (heading, text, mouse-pointer-click, minus, move-vertical, panel-bottom) fell through `BlockIcon`'s `?? SquareDashed`, so the message rail at the top of the email palette drew the same dashed square six times. They are direct named imports in `PageBuilder.tsx` now — the page-builder's own lazy chunk, not the entry. Nothing had asserted it: the kindMeta test checked only that the slug was kebab-shaped, `PageBuilder.stories.tsx` carries no `vrt` tag so VRT never screenshots the template, and axe cannot see a glyph `BlockIcon` marks `aria-hidden`. `page-builder.test.tsx` now renders every palette row on every doc type and fails on a placeholder the slug did not ask for.
history.andTheIgnoreListCanGoBlindToo: An entry that stops matching stops excluding, and the names it was hiding return to the entry with nothing in the log to say why — the same failure mode `blindSources` already guards for STRICT_SOURCES. So a missing file, or one with no `icon:` literals left to skip, fails the generator by name rather than showing up weeks later as an unexplained red ratchet.

history.by: the i18n namespace split: `studio` is fetched by the Studio, for every locale including en-US
history.measured: 296,487 bytes (289.5 KiB gz), down from 311,807 measured on the same inputs — 15.0 KiB gz out of the entry, and 60.5 KiB under the 350 KiB v1.0 target.
history.why: The gate was RED by 80 bytes: the add-on catalogue gained 14 entries and the 2,000-byte margin left on 2026-08-27 had already been spent by an earlier 51. The remedy this file prints — defer the addition — was structurally unavailable, because the addition was fourteen STRINGS: `packages/i18n` bundled all five en-US namespaces into every consumer's entry chunk, so any key any page added landed there no matter how lazy the page was. That is the split the 2026-08-18 record below called out and deliberately did not do.
history.whatItActuallyIs: NOT 'delete the en-US catalogue', which is what 48.7 KiB gz measured and what the fallbacks-reconciliation warning was about. `common.studio.*` and `common.studioPages.*` — 971 keys, ~36 KiB of the en-US bundle, the entire admin console — are the `studio` namespace now, and `studio` is in neither the bundled en-US set nor the initial `ns` list. `StudioBody` (studio/routes.tsx) awaits it through the same spinner the lazy route body already shows. It is the split `resources/index.ts` promised in its own header from the first wave: 'the studio/generated lazy split lands later'.
history.andOneLineInTheBarrel: Moving the keys was worth 46 KB raw and the entry did not shrink at all — it GREW by 0.5 KiB gz. `packages/i18n/src/index.ts` re-exported `EN_US_RESOURCES`, and the note directly above that export had predicted exactly this: Rollup does not drop a re-export's module just because nothing references it. Worse, keeping `resources/index.js` statically reachable also pinned `overrides.ts`'s DYNAMIC import of the same module into the entry, because a module that is statically reachable cannot be split out. Deleting the one line is 15 of the 15.0 KiB. The lesson from 2026-08-18 holds and gained a corollary: attribute the chunk, and attribute it AGAIN after the change, because a structural split that the bundler quietly undoes measures as a regression, not as a no-op.
history.headroom: 1,556 bytes. Set at 2,000 — the usual minifier-drift margin, not growth room — and 444 of it was spent the same day regenerating `packages/ui/src/components/icon/icon-core.ts`, which the page-builder's six new `email.*` block slugs had made stale (five icons genuinely new; `Minus` was already in the entry via `Checkbox.tsx`). Those icons are entry weight nothing renders: the page-builder resolves block glyphs through its own local `BLOCK_ICONS` map in `PageBuilder.tsx`, never through the catalogue, so `gen-icon-core.mjs`'s best-effort `icon:` sweep is over-collecting exactly as its own docblock warns. Attributing all 144 emitted names to their collecting source finds EIGHTEEN whose only origin is `packages/widgets/src/templates/page-builder/builder-config.ts` — today's six and twelve already shipping — worth ~2.1 KiB gz, more than the headroom left. Their surface is `EmailTemplatesPage`, one of the eleven routes this file's 2026-08-18 record moved behind React.lazy. Excluding that one file from the generic scan is the follow-up, and it is NOT this change; hand-editing icon-core.ts is not an option, because `icon-core.test.ts` re-runs the generator's `--check`.
history.cost: One chunk on the first Studio surface a session opens: ~17 KiB gz for en-US. A locale other than en-US fetches two (its own and the en-US fallback behind it) where it previously fetched one and carried the English inline — so it is ahead by ~15 KiB on every route and behind by ~17 KiB on the Studio it may never open. Nothing else changed: the boot path makes no new request, because `studio` is not in the initial `ns` list.
history.whatItCost: Three obligations, all now gated by `apps/dashboard/src/i18n/studioNamespace.test.ts`: every `studio:` key must exist in the bundle, every one must be paired with an inline fallback that MATCHES it character for character (the fallback is what renders between the route opening and the chunk landing, and in every unit test that never boots i18next — one had drifted), and nothing outside `src/studio` may read the namespace (the Topbar did, on every route, so it has its own `topbar.*` keys now). The override rows moved with the messages in meta migration 0022.

history.by: lazy-loading the self-host first-run wizard off the /setup route
history.measured: 309,727 bytes (302.5 KiB gz), down from 313,583 measured on the same inputs — 3.8 KiB gz out of the entry, 47.5 KiB under the 350 KiB v1.0 target.
history.why: The connection-pause wave added ~0.2 KiB gz of genuinely entry-resident weight (18 en-US strings in the eagerly-bundled `common` catalogue, and the 13th system state) and the gate went red by 183 bytes — the 1,956-byte margin left on 2026-08-24 had already been spent by ordinary additions since. Attributing the entry source map (the 2026-08-18 lesson: attribute, never infer from the changelog) found `app/router.tsx` importing `SetupPage` statically, which put `FirstRunWizard` and `TelemetryConsent` (3,869 + 3,171 raw attributed bytes) in the synchronous set for every user on every route. That wizard runs ONCE per instance, before anybody has an account, and its own route guard redirects to /login the moment a super admin exists — so on a configured install it is the one screen a returning user provably cannot reach, and everybody was downloading it anyway. Its desktop twin `/desktop/setup` was already lazy; this is the same click.
history.headroom: 2,000 bytes — the usual minifier-drift margin, not growth room.

history.notAnException: The static set is deliberately the FIRST PAINT — auth screens, AppShell, HomePage, PageRenderer, the system states, the 404 (see the note above `lazyRoute` in app/router.tsx). /setup is not first paint for a returning user; it is unreachable for one.

history.by: deferring the two data-io route bodies, which is what finally made the page-wizard template split real
history.measured: 315,684 bytes (308.3 KiB gz), down from 330,905 on the same build inputs — 14.9 KiB gz out of the entry, and 42.7 KiB under the 350 KiB v1.0 target.
history.why: `app/router.tsx` imports `data-io/routes.tsx` statically — it has to, the routes are built at module scope — and that module imported `ImportWizardPage` and `DataExportsPage` statically, so both route bodies were in the synchronously-loaded set for every user on every route. `ImportWizardPage` is ALSO the `page-wizard` template body, so the lazy binding `pages/templates.tsx` registers for `page-wizard` was a NO-OP: its chunk held a 22-line wrapper while the body shipped on boot regardless. Thirteen of the fourteen template bindings were genuinely deferred and the accounting said fourteen. Both are deferred now, so both are what they claim to be.

whatMoved.ImportWizardPage: the bulk of it: the wizard pulls @adminium/widgets' PageWizard, UploadDropzone, ColumnMappingTableWidget and ValidationIssuesListWidget along with their zod config schemas.
whatMoved.DataExportsPage: the exports manager, a route body with no second life as a template.

history.headroom: 2,016 bytes — the same margin the click below left, and for the same reason: enough to absorb minifier drift, not enough to hide growth.
history.cost: One chunk fetch the first time /imports or /exports is opened. The page surface and its topbar title stay outside the Suspense boundary, so the frame paints on the first frame and only the body waits behind a centered spinner.
history.whatThisNumberIsNot: The gate builds its asset list from two regexes that both hardcode `\.js`, so the entry STYLESHEET is uncounted: `index.css` is a plain <link> in <head> with no media trick and blocks paint. Measured on this build it is 20,955 bytes gz, which puts the real blocking payload at 336,639 against the 358,400 target — 21,761 bytes of room, not 42,716. Widening the gate to count CSS (and the self-hosted woff2 faces, also uncounted) is a separate change; recording the number here is so the JS figure is not read as the whole story.
history.drift: The 331,000 this came down from was already loose: a fresh build measured 330,905 before this change, against the 329,014 the record below pinned. Nothing raised the ratchet — ordinary additions spent the margin (60 locale keys and two now-static icons on 2026-08-19, then 20 SMTP + export strings on 2026-08-20, ~1.4 KiB gz between them), which is exactly the drift a ratchet is meant to make visible and a stale one hides. RELEASE-GATE.md now states this measurement in both places it records the entry chunk.

history.by: lazy-loading the page templates and the non-first-paint routes, and removing the lucide barrel
history.measured: 329,014 bytes (321.3 KiB gz), down from 670,786 — a 51% reduction. **Under the 350 KiB v1.0 target for the first time.**
history.why: The four raises of 2026-08-17 and the note below them all attributed this gate's growth to the en-US i18n catalogue and named the namespace split as the fix — 'the single highest-leverage item', 'it would return all three of today's raises and then some'. That was measured for the first time on 2026-08-18 and it is wrong. Deleting EN_US_RESOURCES entirely and rebuilding gives 48.7 KiB gz: real, a seventh of what was actually available, and nowhere near a 305 KiB gap. Attributing the entry chunk's own source map instead found the weight in three places nobody had looked at.

whatItActuallyWas.1. page templates, -97.0 KiB gz: `pages/templates.tsx` statically imported all fourteen page-template bindings, and each pulls a template component out of @adminium/widgets. A page renders exactly ONE template, so thirteen were downloaded by every user on every route and never executed. `resolvePageTemplate` was already async and `TemplateMount` already rendered a skeleton for its resolving phase — the machinery was built and then fed a synchronous map.
whatItActuallyWas.2. the lucide barrel, -112.6 KiB gz: `packages/ui`'s `Icon` and the dashboard's `lucideByName` both resolved an icon from a runtime name via `import { icons } from 'lucide-react'`. A map lookup is opaque to a bundler, so all 1,611 icon modules were emitted — verified in the source map, all 1,611 with non-zero attributed bytes — for the ~136 the product draws. `scripts/gen-icon-core.mjs` now emits those as named imports; the full catalogue is a dynamic import that only a hand-picked icon outside the set pulls in.
whatItActuallyWas.3. route components, -62.7 KiB gz: Eleven route components were statically imported in `app/router.tsx`, so they were in the synchronously-loaded set on every route. `EmailTemplatesPage` was the expensive one by an order of magnitude: it shares the block canvas with `page-builder`, so importing it reached `PageBuilder` → `WidgetHost` → the whole widget REGISTRY, 23 families of definitions and Zod config schemas, 336 KiB minified. The rest — About, API keys, Changelog, KB, Account, Preferences, Notifications, Defaults, Desktop settings, Desktop setup, Onboarding — are ordinary admin screens.

history.whatWasDeliberatelyNotDone: Removing the en-US catalogue from the entry, i.e. the thing the previous entries recommended. It is worth 48.7 KiB gz and the target no longer needs it, but it is not free: `t(key, fallback)` passes the fallback as i18next's `defaultValue`, so en-US would render from the CALL SITES instead of the catalogue — and comparing all 2,052 single-quoted call sites against `common.json` found five that have drifted. Two of them are the catalogue carrying an ICU plural (`{count, plural, one {# column} other {# columns}}`) where the fallback is a bare `{count} columns`, so the swap would ship '1 columns'. The catalogue is authoritative in those places and the fallbacks are stale; reconciling them is real work, and it is not a bundle-size task.
history.headroom: 1,986 bytes (~1.9 KiB). Wider than the ~400 the raise entries left, because the ratchet is no longer the binding constraint — the v1.0 target is 27 KiB below it and that is what should be defended now.
history.cost: One chunk fetch the first time a page of a given template is opened, and one the first time an admin screen is opened — both behind the <Suspense> fallbacks those routes already rendered. The first paint (auth screens, AppShell, HomePage, PageRenderer, the system states, the 404) is untouched and stays static by design.

supersededHistory.note: Six raise/lower entries from 2026-08-04 to 2026-08-17 lived here in full. They are dropped rather than kept, because four of them recorded the same wrong diagnosis in increasing detail and leaving them would preserve the reasoning that produced four raises in one day. The record that matters is above: what was believed, what was measured, and the difference.
supersededHistory.theLesson: Every one of those entries reasoned about the cause from what had just been added — 'this feature added 110 strings, the entry grew, therefore strings' — and none attributed the chunk it was measuring. The entry's own source map answers the question directly in about a minute, and it named three causes none of which were the one four consecutive entries agreed on.
supersededHistory.gitHistory: The full text is in git history for apps/dashboard/chunk-budget.json before 2026-08-18.
